svg.title: Drugs for blood cancers: classic cytotoxic classes (alkylating agents, antimetabolites, topoisomerase inhibitors, antimicrotubule agents) hit every dividing cell and each has an organ toxicity to watch; targeted and immune therapies (monoclonal antibodies and CAR-T cells, small molecules, checkpoint inhibitors) are matched to one molecule on the tumour

svg.text: Systemic therapy for a blood cancer: hit EVERY dividing cell, or ONE target on the tumour?

svg.text: surgery only DIAGNOSES (resect a node) · radiation treats locally: see the RADIATION ONCOLOGY chart

svg.text: glucocorticoids (prednisone, dexamethasone) kill lymphoid cells: lymphomas, chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), acute B-cell

svg.text: leukemia, myeloma · also shrink swelling around metastases
